newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - AccuStaff comfortable on EPS.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - AccuStaff comfortable on EPS.

text.p: AccuStaff Inc chief executive Derek Dewan said he was "absolutely" comfortable with the Wall Street consensus estimate of about $0.98 for this year.
In an interview with Reuters, Dewan said the consensus of about $1.20 for next year was also in line. The company had pro forma results of $0.35 in 1996.

DeWan said that, contrary to a report in the current edition of Barron's newspaper, the company has had strong internal growth, which he estimated at about 22 percent in the first quarter versus a year ago.
He said that core growth, from August, 1994, before its initial public offering, through the end of 1996, was in the high 20-percent range.
Dewan said it was "absolutely not true" that the company was suffering a temporary cash drain, as Barron's reported in "Up and Down Wall Street" column.
He said the company has been collecting its accounts receivable in 30 to 60 days, with the average around 45 days.
Dewan acknowledged that the company has used up much of its cash on hand for acquisitions, but said the "money was spent wisely."
Barron's noted that the goodwill line on its balance sheet has grown to about $580 million out of almost $700 million in shareholder equity as acquisitions have increased.
Dewan said that the valuation of goodwill was "within a conservative range."
